newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bourse says no market cooling plans.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bourse says no market cooling plans.

text.p: Prices on the Shanghai Stock Exchange are running relatively high but the exchange has no plans to introduce measures to cool the market down, exchange president Yang Xianghai said on Tuesday.
"I think this is a market problem. This exchange does not have any plans to push down market prices," Yang told Reuters in an interview.
He said prices had risen sharply since the beginning of 1997 and were now at "relatively high" levels.
"Under such conditions, the only way is to strengthen supervision over the market," he said. "At the same time, all departments are now carrying out education about risk.
"I think we must use these measures to make the market develop in a healthy manner," Yang said. He gave no further details.
Prices on the Shanghai Stock Exchange have risen sharply since the beginning of the year, causing fears the central government might intervene to stop speculation and cool down the market.
